title: A comparison of decimals of different scales casts both sides to one DECIMAL(38, s) and raises on a value that does not fit
verdict: `overflow: ERROR` native; the writer does not emit the native comparison across scales
description: `DECIMAL(38,0) > DECIMAL(38,10)` casts both sides to `DECIMAL(38,10)`, the larger scale at 38 digits. A value with more than `38 - s` integer digits does not fit: `99999999999999999999999999999999999999::DECIMAL(38,0) > 1.5::DECIMAL(38,10)` raises `Conversion Error: Casting value ... to type DECIMAL(38,10) failed: value is out of range!`, for `=` as for `>`. Values that fit compare exactly (`1.5 > 1` and `1 = 1.0` are true).
The docs are silent on the common type of a comparison across scales: a docs gap.
reference: The reference compares the exact values, with no issue (D31 does not apply: decimals have one representation). DuckDB's own comparison raises where the common type does not fit, so the writer does not emit it across scales (below).

The DuckDB writer does not emit the native comparison across scales: `Dialect.decimal_compare` brings both sides to integers (the integer part times `10ˢ` plus the fraction times `10ˢ`, in `HUGEINT`) and compares those with floor division, so no implicit cast runs (#1498).

provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations` runs each query on a fresh connection and records the rows or the error as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current.
